sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 1.5% a year from $41.9 billion in FY2016 to $47.9 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F219], a flat decade that hides two large restructurings.
The first inflection was FY2017, when revenue fell 13.5% [D42] and net income fell 80.9% to $1.2 billion [F52][D44] on a 82.5% effective tax rate [D28].
The second was FY2025, when operating income jumped 37.7% to $13.8 billion [F40][D450] and operating margin rose 7.5pp to 28.7% [F50][D463].

The FY2025 step-up came primarily from lower other operating charges after the prior-year fairlife contingent-consideration remeasurement, plus 1% concentrate volume growth and favorable pricing [P12].
In FY2025 concentrate operations contributed 1.6pp of the 1.9% revenue growth [D534][D449], lifting their share to 59.4% of revenue [D532].
Finished product operations added only 0.3pp [D541], with US finished product up 6.5% [D561] offset by a 4.9% decline outside the US [D554].
By geography, the US contributed 1.6pp of growth [D525] while non-US added just 0.2pp [D484], so the US now carries 39.9% of revenue [D523].
Profit grew far faster than revenue: operating income rose 37.7% against 1.9% revenue growth [D450][D449], an incremental margin of 428.4% [D473].
Diluted EPS rose 23.6% [D453] against 23.3% net income growth [D451], with the diluted share count down only 0.2% [D468].
Operating margin of 28.7% in FY2025 [F50] sits above the 26.0% window median [D766] and is the window high [D765], against a low of 20.7% in FY2016 [D764].
Gross margin rose 0.6pp to 61.6% [F30][D462], within a 58.1% to 62.1% window range [D770][D771].
The gross margin gain came from favorable pricing and the prior-year refranchising, partly offset by currency and higher commodity costs [P14].
The FY2025 operating-margin bridge is dominated by a 6.2pp residual from other lines [D477], with cost of revenue adding 0.6pp [D475] and SG&A 0.7pp [D476].
Net margin of 27.3% [F70] sits just 1.4pp below operating margin [F50], helped by a 17.9% effective tax rate [D435] and $1.1 billion of other income [X100].
Operating cash flow of $7.4 billion [F100] was only 0.57x net income [D436], and free cash flow of $5.3 billion [F120] just 0.40x [D437], the window low [D776] against a 0.97x median [D778].

FY2024's collapse to $6.8 billion [F99] was driven primarily by the $6.0 billion IRS Tax Litigation Deposit [P22], and FY2025's $603 million recovery came from stronger operating results and lower tax payments [P1].
Free cash flow margin of 11.0% [D433] is far below the 20.2% window median [D775], and capex at 4.4% of revenue [D432] now runs 2.01x D&A [D438].
Stock-based compensation is small at 3.8% of operating cash flow [D439], so working capital and tax timing, not compensation, explain the weak conversion.
Net cash of $8.8 billion [D442] equals 18.3% of revenue [D443], in the 100th percentile of six staples peers against a -14.5% peer median [D793][D794].
That position flipped from net debt of $32.4 billion in FY2023 [D341], and the current ratio of 1.46x is the window high [F200][D780].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.5 billion [D444] were 179.9% of free cash flow [D445], the third straight year above 100% [D344][D395].
Dividends alone were $8.8 billion [X145] while buybacks fell to $746 million [X135], and the diluted share count barely moved, down 0.2% [D468].

Revenue for FY2017 and FY2018 in the table is a later recast, $36.2 billion and $34.3 billion versus $35.4 billion and $31.9 billion first reported [F2][X2][F3][X3], so growth spanning those years mixes presentations [R1].
Payouts exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 [D344][D395][D445], a three-year pattern that leans on the balance sheet [R2].
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2024 and FY2025 [D387][D437], ranking 0th percentile against a 0.94x peer median [D795][D796] [R3].
Total debt rose 31.3% in FY2025 [D470] to $1.5 billion [D441], though from a near-zero base after the prior-year 97.3% decline [D420] [R4].
Free cash flow to net income: a move back toward the 0.97x window median [D778] from 0.40x [D437] would confirm the cash recovery; the FY2026 10-K cash flow section is where it appears.
Operating margin: holding above the 26.0% window median [D766] after the 28.7% FY2025 peak [F50] would show the other-charges benefit was not one-off; watch the FY2026 MD&A margin discussion.

Buybacks plus dividends against free cash flow: a fall from 179.9% [D445] toward the 105.1% level of FY2023 [D344] would signal the payout is being re-based to cash generation; watch the FY2026 financing cash flow lines.
